assembly_instructions: Set four 4x4 in lower frame rails on stands: port and starboard longitudinal rails first, then bolt the front and rear crossmembers between them to form the rectangular base.
Bolt the middle deck crossmember and thin operator deck plate to the lower rails, leaving the four wheel-hub bays open for hydraulic motor service.
Install the four vertical corner posts and bolt the two upper side rails to their tops, completing the bolted XYZ space frame.
Mount the rear tool bar and three-point hitch lugs to the rear crossmember before installing rear wheels, because the hitch bolts pass through the rear frame bay.

Bolt each hub motor bracket to its corner of the space frame, slide the hydraulic universal-rotor motor and planetary gear-down into the bracket, then install the steel rim and rubber tire at all four corners.

Assemble the removable PowerCube on its skid: engine block, hydraulic pump, reservoir, radiator, fuel tank, exhaust stack, hose manifold, and labelled quick-coupler blocks; lower the skid onto the rear upper rails and bolt it down.
Install the operator station by bolting the seat base to the deck, adding the cushion, backrest, foot plate, steering column, and joystick valve console.
Bolt the ROPS posts to the upper rails, add the top crossbar and two diagonal braces, then verify the seat is inside the rollover envelope.
Attach the front loader pivot brackets to the forward posts, insert the main pivot pins, and hang the left and right loader arms with the cross tube square to both arms.

Pin each lift-cylinder barrel eye to the lower frame clevis, extend the chrome rod to the loader-arm clevis, insert the upper rod pin, and check that both cylinder axes align between their two pin centers.
Build the bucket as an open scoop from the sloped floor, angled rear shell segments, rolled top back strip, side cheeks, cutting edge, tooth bar, and bottom wear strips.
Bolt the quick-attach plate to the bucket rear plate, install the lower bucket pins and top latch bar, then pin the assembly to both loader arms.

Route four drive hoses to the hub motors plus two lift hoses to the loader cylinders through the visible manifold and quick-coupler blocks, then pressure-test the hydraulic system before fitting rear implements.

info.japanese_name: ライフトラック（オープンソース・トラクター）
info.summary: Bolt-together, open-source, four-wheel hydraulic skid-steer tractor. Foundational workhorse of OSE's 50-machine Global Village Construction Set.
info.description: LifeTrac is a modular, open-source tractor developed by Open Source Ecology as the prime mover of its Global Village Construction Set. The entire machine is built from bolted 4×4 in square steel tubing — a 'XYZ space frame' — so individual modules (wheels, PowerCube, loader arm, tool bar) can be swapped in the field without welding. Each of the four wheels is driven independently by a hydraulic universal-rotor hub motor through a planetary gear-down, enabling true skid-steer turning and four-wheel independent traction. Hydraulic power comes from a removable PowerCube engine/pump module mounted on the rear of the chassis; flows are distributed via quick-couplers to the loader-arm cylinders, the drive motors, and any attached implement. The front loader has two parallel arms pivoting at the front posts with two hydraulic cylinders lifting them; the arms terminate at a universal quick-attach plate that carries the bucket. The rear universal tool bar accepts rippers, three-point hitches, augers, and backhoes. All CAD, bill of materials, and build instructions are released under CC BY-SA 4.0.
info.operator: Open Source Ecology and community builders (farms, training sites, maker communities)
